transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I can’t seem to stop worrying about everything all at once. My marriage, whether I’m slipping at work, bills, projects around the house I keep not finishing... and whether I’m failing as a husband and father.
Roughly how long have you been experiencing this constant worry?
About nine months now. It really started when the cloud migration at work ramped up, and the arguments at home started happening regularly.
Alongside all this worry, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or depressed most days?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I know I’ve been under a lot of pressure, but I haven’t really thought of it as being depressed.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy doing?
I’m not sure I’ve really noticed that. I still want to do the things I usually enjoy; it’s more that I have a hard time relaxing enough to focus on them.
Have you noticed any physical tension in your body, like tight or aching muscles?

Yeah, definitely. I feel wound tight almost all day—my shoulders feel locked up, like I’m bracing for something. I’ll catch myself pacing between meetings, or tapping at chess club, because sitting still feels almost impossible.
Have you been having trouble falling or staying asleep, or experiencing restless sleep?

Yeah. Most nights I’m exhausted, but once I’m in bed my mind just keeps going—work risks, money, things I said to my wife. And even if I fall asleep, I’ll wake up around three or four and then I can’t really get back to sleep because I’m already thinking through tomorrow’s problems.
Have you noticed yourself feeling unusually irritable or short-tempered with others recently?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself being especially short-tempered with people.
